title: Humans above the Arctic Circle (Yana)
summary: The Yana site, about 32,000 years old, is among the earliest evidence of people living north of the Arctic Circle, with perhaps the earliest clear evidence of mammoth hunting.
why: Shows humans could survive the high Arctic in the Ice Age.

notes.problem: Disputed 'earliest': the catalog's own migration source says humans 'reached sites in Arctic Russia by 40,000 years ago'; Yana page hedges mammoth hunting ('perhaps').

superlativeSource: provides perhaps the earliest unambiguous evidence of mammoth hunting by humans
